bw: Child with fever, seizure lasting over 5 minutes
w: Phenobarbital is a second-line agent after benzodiazepines.
Fosphenytoin is second line if seizures persist after benzodiazepines.
p: Status epilepticus (seizure above 5 minutes): IV lorazepam first, then fosphenytoin, levetiracetam or valproate.

bw: Electric facial pain triggered by touch or shaving
w: Cluster headache causes periorbital pain with tearing, not touch-triggered lancinating pain.
Migraine is throbbing with photophobia and nausea rather than brief electric pain.
p: Trigeminal neuralgia: brief paroxysms in V2/V3 triggered by light touch; carbamazepine is first-line, and MRI looks for vascular compression.

bw: Teen with pharyngitis, cervical nodes, splenomegaly
Weeks of fatigue, similar cases at school
w: Throat culture detects group A strep, which does not cause splenomegaly and prolonged fatigue.
HIV ELISA would be considered only if mononucleosis-like illness persists with Monospot negative.
p: Infectious mononucleosis (EBV): heterophile antibody (Monospot) is the first test; atypical lymphocytes and avoid contact sports for splenic rupture risk.

w: Metformin improves insulin resistance but is second line for cycle regulation.
Spironolactone treats hirsutism and needs contraception, and it does not protect the endometrium.
p: PCOS: combined oral contraceptives regulate cycles, reduce androgens and protect against endometrial hyperplasia.

w: Coronaviruses usually cause mild upper respiratory illness in infants.
Streptococcus pneumoniae causes lobar pneumonia, not wheezy bronchiolitis.
p: RSV is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in infants under 2; palivizumab prophylaxis is for high-risk preterm infants.

w: Alprazolam is a benzodiazepine with dependence risk and is not first line.
Propranolol treats somatic performance anxiety but does not treat generalized anxiety.
p: Generalized anxiety disorder: SSRIs or SNRIs plus CBT are first-line; buspirone is an alternative, benzodiazepines only short term.

bw: Prior eye pain and blurred vision (uveitis)
w: Methotrexate is ineffective for axial spondyloarthritis.
Cyclophosphamide is not used for ankylosing spondylitis.
p: Ankylosing spondylitis is treated first with NSAIDs and exercise, then TNF-alpha or IL-17 inhibitors if inadequate.

x: screening recommendation depends on guideline version

bw: 3 days of vomiting after every meal
w: Anion gap acidosis follows ketoacidosis or toxins, not loss of gastric acid.
Respiratory acidosis with hyperkalemia suggests hypoventilation, not vomiting.
p: Vomiting loses gastric H+ and Cl-, causing hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis; volume depletion raises aldosterone and worsens hypokalemia.

bw: Thumb numbness, cannot make OK sign
w: Scaphoid fractures cause snuffbox tenderness in young adults, not neurologic signs in children.
Distal radius fractures cause wrist pain and deformity and spare the anterior interosseous nerve.
p: Supracondylar fracture in children can injure the anterior interosseous nerve (inability to make an OK sign) and the brachial artery.

bw: Disinhibition: undressing, putting objects in mouth
w: Alzheimer disease begins with memory loss, with personality preserved early.
Lewy body dementia causes visual hallucinations, parkinsonism and fluctuating cognition.
p: Frontotemporal dementia (Pick disease): early behavioral change and disinhibition; Pick bodies (tau) and frontotemporal atrophy.

bw: Salmon patch with collarette, then Christmas-tree rash
w: Systemic steroids are unnecessary for a self-limited eruption.
Phototherapy is an option only for severe or prolonged disease.
p: Pityriasis rosea: herald patch then truncal papules along skin lines; resolves in 6-8 weeks; consider syphilis serology if atypical.

w: Acanthocytes appear in abetalipoproteinemia and liver disease.
Schistocytes indicate microangiopathic hemolysis or mechanical valves.
p: The spleen removes nuclear remnants (Howell-Jolly bodies) from red cells; they signal splenectomy or autosplenectomy and need vaccination against encapsulated organisms.

w: Maternal alcohol use causes fetal alcohol syndrome with microcephaly, not polycythemia.
Neonatal Listeria infection causes sepsis or meningitis with granulomas and no polycythemia.
p: Infants of diabetic mothers have polycythemia, hypoglycemia, macrosomia and congenital heart disease; hyperviscosity can cause thrombosis and seizures.

w: Ceftriaxone alone misses resistant pneumococci, so vancomycin is added.
Ampicillin for Listeria is added only above age 50 or with immunosuppression.
p: Empiric meningitis therapy in adults under 50: ceftriaxone plus vancomycin (plus dexamethasone); add ampicillin if over 50 or immunocompromised.

w: Vasodilators such as captopril and diuretics can worsen hypotension in aortic stenosis and give no survival benefit.
Nitroprusside is a vasodilator for hypertensive emergencies, not definitive therapy.
p: Symptomatic severe aortic stenosis is treated with surgical or transcatheter valve replacement; medical therapy does not improve survival.
